thread.title: Apple’s Path to $1 Trillion Is Paved With iPhones, Upbeat Guidance

author: Jon Swartz
title: Apple’s Path to $1 Trillion Is Paved With iPhones, Upbeat Guidance
text:
By Jon Swartz Aug. 1, 2018 1:20 p.m. ET Fresh off its best-ever fiscal third quarter, Apple (AAPL) closed in on $1 trillion in market value with shares rising 5.3% on Wednesday. The stock just cracked the $200-per-share barrier.
In its inexorable path to become the first U.S.-based company to reach $1 trillion, Apple has as much to thank its fiscal-fourth-quarter guidance as its recently completed June quarter.
Illustration: Apple Inc. The Cupertino, Calif.-based company on Tuesday forecast Q4 revenue between $60 billion and $62 billion , easily topping analyst estimates of $59.4 billion.
"We expect the vast majority of Apple's product lineup to be refreshed during the next couple of quarters, which should support near-term results," Shannon Cross of Cross Research wrote in a note to clients.
Investors should expect a bump in iPhone sales in the fiscal fourth quarter, when Apple is expected to unfurl three new phones in September, followed by a blockbuster fiscal first quarter during the holiday-shopping season.
"We see more upside than downside risk to the upcoming iPhone product cycle and a building services narrative," Morgan Stanley analyst Katy Huberty wrote in a report. "Even if device revenue growth slows, services and wearables can pick up the slack, delivering 5% revenue and 14% EPS growth annually through 2020."
Daniel Ives , head of technology research at GBH Insights , believes the trio of new iPhones "will capture the underlying demand/upgrades among customers that have decided to bypass the [iPhone] 8/8+/X cycle this past time around, with price points and features that catalyze fence-sitting iPhone customers onto their next smartphone during the course of 2018 and [first-half] 2019 with Chinese consumers front and center."
This should put to rest any lingering concerns about flat iPhone unit shipments, which caused Apple to slip to No. 3 in world-wide smartphone market share behind Huawei Technologies , the new No. 2, and leader Samsung Electronics (South Korea: 005930), according to market researcher IDC .
Yet more than a decade after its debut, iPhone remains the engine for 60% of the company's revenue. True, unit shipments have tapered off of late, but a burgeoning digital-services business ($9.55 billion) and gadgets built around the smartphone have contributed to Apple's revenue stream. That, and higher iPhone prices (a record average selling price of $724), led to a 20% jump in iPhone-related revenue ($29.9 billion) year-over-year.
